newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast spot products flat amid thin volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast spot products flat amid thin volume.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast products were unchanged in Thursday trade, amid ample supply and little demand as traders attended an industry function, players said.
NYMEX crude oil failed to give West Coast spot trade a lift, rising 30 cents a barrel to $20.03 Thursday on reports a Kurdish faction arrested United Nations oil monitors in northern Iraq.
Adequate supply soured trader interest in the futures rise, with stocks up 578,000 barrels to 26.7 million barrels last week, according to the American Petroleum Institute.
Rising supplies were also reflected in refinery use, which rose 0.8 percentage points last week to 92.1 percent of capacity.
April/May prices for ultra-clean CARB gasoline were unchanged from Wednesday at 70/71 cents a gallon, while San Francisco CARB was pegged 1.50 cents less.
Conventional unleaded gasoline for prompt delivery stood 66/67 cents.
Distillates eased Thursday, with buyers of CARB low sulphur diesel traded around 68/68/50 cents a barrel.
